doc.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Her place in the piano lineage: Cleo Brown and Lil Armstrong
summary: Asked about the piano lineage, she names Lil Armstrong and Cleo Brown, a great pianist few knew, whom she tracked down.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: [laughs]. Let me see. What do you see yourself in terms of the jazz piano lineage? If . . .

We know who some of your heroes and heroines were, and people who came before you, whether it was Mary Lou and perhaps Milt Buckner or different ones like that. Names I’d like to mention that people don’t know . . .
Lil Armstrong. Who? . . . O.k., so are there a few other names out there . . .
Cleo Laine. I’m sorry. I don’t mean Cleo Laine.
I’m sorry. I mean Cleo Brown.
What a great piano player, and that nobody ever knew she existed.
Yeah. You told her about, told me about her. You told her about me. Right. [laughs]
I probably would have told her about you too. She was something. I was . . . There’s another person I absolutely knocked my brains out to find.
Tracked her down. People kept saying, “She’s dead.” No. Then I tracked her down.
She was around then. O.k. So there’s some names . . . Are there any others before you that, maybe names like that you can now be the voice for the voiceless, so to speak.
